answer: Per-epoch memory-hard proofs make every fake key pay rent. Each key must publish an umber, a proof from a 2 GB memory-hard puzzle seeded by the epoch hash, costing about 0.4 POA of compute; a key without a fresh umber loses its reward slot. One machine cannot batch proofs, because the spiral, a sequential memory walk, fills the 2 GB of its island, a single machine. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 islands x 0.4 POA = 400 POA per epoch, so 100 epochs cost 40,000 POA. Attacker pays 40,000 POA.
